calls.reason: Ramp documents widespread business payments, and NVIDIA describes simulation uses. Neither establishes the scale of alternative workloads or whether paid AI demand survives without subsidies and circular financing.

Tom’s Guide reports subsidies for heavy users but says typical subscribers remain profitable. The survey counts users, not compute; neither source establishes the claimed overwhelming compute share or unaffordability.
CARMA documents changing AI coverage, with innovation and productivity still dominating headlines. It does not establish that promotion has subsided or measure durable demand after that happens.

ARC Prize and METR demonstrate bounded autonomous planning and action, while METR also reports open-ended reasoning weaknesses. This leaves the undefined broader capability unsettled and cannot establish that it will never arrive.
